source.text: first the date of birth ... Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. ... Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year. ... `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss.

source.text: 32. If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks for a new payment plan or lower instalments.

source.text: 10. A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41). Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`. On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.

source.text: The outcome table of Brief A applies. With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`. Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`. With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above. (Brief A: If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason. 47. Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.)

1. `get_account` returns one to three products. 2. State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything. 4. First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. ... Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. 10. ... Promises recorded before the request stay.

unresolved.text: The brief describes the content of the first sentence (digital assistant, Freya Bank, call is recorded) but gives no exact wording and does not require it word for word; the opening is a first-person rendering of that description.
Rule 17 says to say you are calling from the collections team about a late payment, without exact wording; rendered in first person.
Brief B rule 4 says to ask whether the customer can pay all of them today, without exact wording.
Rule 13 says to ask the customer to say the month as a word; no exact wording given.
These replies are given as indirect speech ('say that ...'); they are first-person renderings, not verbatim sentences.

Brief B rule 9 lets only dispute and already-paid continue with the other products; it does not say whether hardship (declined transfer) or a refusal to talk notes every remaining product and closes. Modelled as closing (Brief A rules 32 and 45: close as no_promise / hardship or refused), with notes per unpromised product (Brief B rule 8).
Rule 32: 'This rule comes before rules 30 and 41.' before_persuasion covers rule 30; the IR has no field for precedence over the restructuring transfer (rule 41).
Rule 45 closes when the customer says twice they do not want to talk; it does not literally say to ask once whether you can help. ask_once_first=true is used to represent the first strike.
Rule 14 says to tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch, without exact wording; failed_instruction is a rendering.
Rule 10: 'A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.' No IR field; must be enforced in prompts.
Rule 33: 'Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.' No IR field; must be enforced in prompts.

Rule 29 (a proposed date or amount is never a refusal), rule 31 (do not repeat an offer already refused), rule 35 (re-check and read back a changed date or amount at confirmation) and Brief B rule 10 (agreed but unrecorded promises are not recorded on a restructuring transfer) have no dedicated IR fields.
The documents do not say how to resolve a promise date given without a month or year (e.g. 'the 20th').
The documents name the security questions (date of birth, last four digits of the phone number on file) but give no exact wording for asking them.
